thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] streaming-prod p99 latency spike detected > 3s across multiple regions. Auto-incident created: 633333. Tags: kv-cache, slab-fragmentation, streaming

mira: observed p95 climbing from ~400ms -> 950ms and p99 hitting 3.4s at 11:03 UTC. Traces show long tail during streaming chunks — stalls rather than uniform slowdown. paging eng-sre + eng-runtime. i'm taking lead.

jon: looking at kv metrics: sudden uptick in `kv.eviction_rate` and `kv.slab_fragmentation_index` around 11:02. prefill_hit dropped 94% -> 55%. decode hitratio is steady. seems like prefill tasks are failing to reuse slabs, causing more small evictions.

hailey: runtime reports elevated prefill worker CPU + GC pauses on nodes n-12 and n-14. those nodes show OOM kills on prefill process most recent 10 minutes. decode workers appear to be queuing while prefill thrashes memory.

mira: customer impact check — samira?

samira: support ingest: ~18 customers reporting streaming pauses > 8s in last 20m, three escalations. Latency errors not causing 5xx broadly, clients are seeing stalls/timeouts for long-running streams. I recommend severity: P1 degraded if number escalates; for now mark P2 and update customers in 15m.

jon: hypothesis: workload shift to longer sequential prompts + increased prefix diversity increased active keys, causing slab fragmentation; prefill tries to allocate and evicts many small ranges instead of reusing existing slabs. Prefill->Decode contention observed: prefill holds memory during allocation and decode waits causing tail.

mira: quick mitigations to run now:
- reduce prefill concurrency on affected pools to 2 workers
- temporarily increase eviction headroom to 20% on hot shards
- roll a runtime config to reduce streaming batch size from 8 -> 5 on canary
- route 20% of traffic to fallback variant with lower prefill (fallback-lite)
- open handoff to infra for slab-defrag scheduling in low-traffic window

ops-bot: command by mira: `infractl kv update --pool streaming-prod-eu --prefill-workers 2 --eviction-headroom 0.20` -> queued.

jon: propose also a short-term decode scale: spin +2 decode pods on affected pools to reduce backpressure while we stabilize.

ops-bot: command by jon: `runtimectl scale --pool streaming-prod-eu --role decode --delta +2` -> accepted.

(3m)
ops-bot: prefill concurrency change applied to streaming-prod-eu (applied by mira).

hailey: saw immediate drop in prefill allocation churn on those nodes. eviction_rate down ~60% on those shards. slab_free rebounded from 8% -> 26% on shard 7 and 31% on shard 9.

mira: canary batch_size rollout to 2 nodes. watching p95/p99.

samira: posted initial customer-facing status update: "Were aware of intermittent streaming pauses affecting a subset of customers and are actively mitigating. Updates in 15 minutes."

jon: added metric filters to alert when `kv.prefill_vs_decode_ratio` crosses threshold; currently prefill tasks were 3x decode memory ops during spike.

(5m)
ops-bot: runtime scale completed: +2 decode pods (jon).

hailey: with decode pods up and prefill throttled, p95 dropped to 480ms and p99 to 1.8s on canary. Production p99 still about 2.2s but trending down. customer reports slowing.

mira: routing change in progress to fallback-lite 20% for 10m.

ops-bot: routerctl: `set-route streaming-prod /variant fallback-lite --percent 20 --duration 10m` -> done.

jon: important log sample showing eviction pattern (from shard=9):
```
2026-04-10T11:02:31Z kv_prefill_alloc shard=9 size=65536 result=alloc
2026-04-10T11:02:32Z kv_prefill_evict shard=9 size=32768 reason=fragmented_free
2026-04-10T11:02:33Z runtime_stream_chunk shard=9 latency=620ms trace_id=abc123
```

mira: note for handoff: if p99 remains >2.5s after 30m, schedule slab-defrag on top-5 shards during maintenance window (expect ~15% throughput degradation for 2-3m per shard).

hailey: medium-term fixes we should track in RFC:
- prefill allocator change to prefer hot-slab reuse and coalesce small frees
- adaptive prefill throttling based on slab_free_percent per-shard
- add earlier alert for prefill_vs_decode imbalance and slab_fragmentation_index

samira: tallying customer impact: ~0.9% of streams impacted over last 30m; 3 premium customers escalated. recommend outreach from solutions tomorrow with incident summary.

product-bot: creating post-incident ticket and scheduling retro with eng-runtime and eng-sre.

mira: handing off to night oncall (jon). key items for handoff:
- monitor `streaming.p99` and `kv.slab_free_percent` (alert if p99 > 2.5s or any shard < 15% free)
- if p99 rises again, run slab-defrag on top-5 shards (coordinate with infra and schedule low-traffic minutes)
- follow up ticket for allocator change and detection alerting

jon: ack, i'll monitor overnight and coordinate defrag if needed. will also keep fallback routing ready to scale up if customer impact resurfaces.

samira: updated customers: final note sent "Mitigation in place; p99 latency improved; targeted follow-up pending."

incident-bot: incident 633333 status: INVESTIGATING -> PARTIALLY MITIGATED by config changes and scaling.

mira: closing thread for handoff. thanks all for quick turn. :heart:
